title: refactor: reuse the shared account menu
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Reuses the SDK-free AccountMenu composition in Enter and AppUserMenu, removing duplicate markup while preserving Enter authentication and sign-out behavior.
- Keeps app connection and account data in the SDK-backed AppUserMenu module. Derives /quests and /pollen links from the SDK's Enter URL; all three app callers and the example now use <AppUserMenu />.
- Uses Connect Pollen, Get free Pollen, Buy Pollen, and Disconnect labels, adds sprout/wallet/link-out icons, and sizes the app dropdown to its contents.
- Passes all 13 UI tests, UI build, formatting, and React showcase/Playground/Websim typechecks; verifies the connected menu and /pollen destination in the local browser. The commit hook could not find lefthook; these checks ran directly.
- Addresses the menu portion of #14470. Dashboard authentication changes remain separate in #14255.

gist.headline: One menu, less pollen
gist.blurb: The account menu stopped growing duplicate little branches across the hive. Enter and the apps now share the same tidy composition, with clearer Pollen actions and a dropdown that fits itself.
gist.summary: Reused the SDK-free AccountMenu composition across Enter and AppUserMenu, while keeping SDK-backed connection data in AppUserMenu and deriving its /quests and /pollen links from the SDK Enter URL.
gist.impact: Users get consistent account menus across Enter, Playground, React showcase, and Websim, including Connect Pollen, Get free Pollen, Buy Pollen, and Disconnect actions with sprout, wallet, and link-out icons.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy shared garden kiosk represents one reusable account-menu component serving several app windows. Polli, wearing a tiny gardener tool belt, tidies one lime-green menu signpost with sprout, wallet, and link-out icons while small connected app screens branch from it; code-plants and flowers reinforce the shared-component/growth metaphor.
